item.title: Molecular Factors Governing Triboelectric Energy Conversion: From Surface Chemistry to Dynamic Charge Transport
item.description: Triboelectric energy conversion has emerged as a promising platform for self-powered electronics, yet its underlying contact electrification mechanisms remain actively debated. In this Perspective, we present a unified framework connecting interfacial chemistry, dielectric physics, transport kinetics, and surface morphology. Taking the contact potential difference (CPD) as a thermodynamic baseline, we examine how chemical functionalization, stoichiometric Fermi-level tuning, and bulk dielectric...

item.title: Ultrafast Radiative Recombination of Singlet Excitons in Conjugated Polymer Aggregates Modulated by the Intrachain Dissociation-Interchain Delocalization Competition
item.description: We readily modulated relaxation pathways of singlet (S1) excitons in push-pull conjugated polymer (CP, D18) aggregates by controlling the spin-coating process. Transient absorption spectroscopy results reveal that intrachain (localized) S1 excitons are efficiently converted into emissive interchain-delocalized excitons in an H-type excitonic coupling-dominant film. Conversely, a notable stimulated emission band emerges and red-shifts toward the steady-state photoluminescence peak within 1 ps in...

item.title: The Role of the Vagus Nerve and Its Stimulation in Modulating Inflammatory Skin Diseases and Other Dermatologic Conditions: From Mechanisms to Therapeutics
item.description: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory skin diseases typically exhibit autonomic imbalance characterized by sympathetic dominance and parasympathetic hypofunction. The vagus nerve plays a fundamental role in modulating inflammatory responses through the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, a neural circuit in which vagal efferent signals lead to acetylcholine release that suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.

item.title: High-Entropy Metal-Organic Frameworks for Water Splitting: Metal-Combination Design and Active-Phase Evolution
item.description: High-entropy metal-organic frameworks (HE-MOFs) are promising water-splitting electrocatalysts because they integrate multiple metals within ordered porous frameworks. However, the mechanistic roles of metal combinations and the identity of the active phase remain unclear. This review summarizes the thermodynamic principles, synthetic strategies, and electrocatalytic applications of HE-MOFs, emphasizing reaction-relevant metal-combination motifs for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and...

item.title: Derivation and Numerical Characterization of a Fractional Quasi-steady-state Approximation for Target-Mediated Drug Disposition Models with History-Dependent Binding
item.description: Standard target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) models describe nonlinear pharmacokinetics arising from high-affinity drug-target interactions but assume that binding depends only on the current drug and target concentrations. Here, we introduce a fractional TMDD model that represents unresolved history dependence in drug-target association through a dimensionally consistent effective concentration based on the Caputo fractional derivative. The formulation preserves conventional kinetic units...

item.title: Development and validation of a voice-based conversational artificial intelligence coaching agent to reduce competitive state anxiety in elite athletes: study protocol for a randomized, analyst-blinded, attention-matched active-controlled trial
item.description: BACKGROUND: Competitive state anxiety harms elite athletes' performance and mental health, while stigma and training demands limit access to face-to-face support; voice-based conversational artificial intelligence (AI) analyzing speech in real time offers a scalable route to psychological skills training (PST).

Strongly donating groups preferentially coordinate to the reactive unsaturated metal and suppress weaker C-H coordination and σ-complex formation required for C-H bond activation. Controlling the initial coordination in photoinduced ligand exchange is therefore one approach to achieving selectivity in bond activation. item.title: Hierarchical Engineering of Atomically Precise Gold Nanoclusters from Alloying to Cluster-Assembled Frameworks
item.description: Atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) provide molecular-level platforms for understanding how atomic structure influences catalytic, photophysical, chiral, and electronic properties. Although alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and nanocluster assembly have each emerged as powerful approaches for tailoring Au NC function, they are often considered as separate design strategies. In this perspective, we organize recent advances in Au NC design across three interconnected levels of...

item.title: Atomic-Scale Unveiling of the True Active Phase of Mn Porphyrin Catalysts on Au(111) Using Electrochemical Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
item.description: Manganese (Mn)-based molecular complexes, inspired by the MnxCay cluster in photosystem II, have been widely investigated as biomimetic catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, it remains unclear whether these molecular catalysts maintain their structural integrity under operating conditions or transform into metal oxide species that serve as the true active sites. Here, we visualize the electrochemical restructuring behavior of Mn porphyrin (MnOEP) monolayers on Au(111) using...

item.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis of host genetics, rumen transcriptome and microbiome prioritizes candidate features associated with body weight in Hanwoo steers
item.description: Hanwoo (Korean cattle) is an indigenous breed of high economic value in Korea, where improving body weight (BW) remains a priority for both productivity and farm profitability. Because growth traits are shaped by multiple biological layers, including host genetics, rumen microbial ecology, and transcriptomic regulation, a single-omics perspective is often insufficient. To address this complexity, we applied an integrative multi-omics framework, DIABLO (Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker...

item.title: Discontinuation of Anticoagulation in Patients at Relatively High Risk of Stroke After Successful Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA(2)DS(2)-VA score 2 to 4.

item.title: Nucleocytoplasmic protein partitioning in plant circadian and plant photobiological processes
item.description: All nuclear proteins require some mechanism to facilitate import from the cytosol into the nucleus. Additionally, many proteins are dually localized, with specific functions and partners within the two compartments. While karyopherins (importins/exportins) generally underlie the basic mechanism of nucleocytoplasmic partitioning, how the members of this large protein family are exploited in specific instances has remained unclear. In this review we survey and update the known instances and...

item.title: Intervention-driven reduction in potentially inappropriate medication use amongst older adults in long-term care facilities in South Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A multidisciplinary medication management programme was associated with reduced medication and PIM use. ED visits and hospitalisations were less frequent in the intervention arm, but not significantly so after accounting for facility-level clustering; the trial was not powered for these events and confirmation is needed.

item.title: Nano-amorphous dispersions with microenvironmental stabilization enable sustained niclosamide solubilization
item.description: Niclosamide suffers from poor oral bioavailability due to acid-induced precipitation and colloidal instability. We developed a nano-stabilized amorphous solid dispersion using PVP-VA and MgO, which maintained supersaturation, suppressed precipitation, and enhanced oral absorption. The formulation improved dissolution (>3-fold) and significantly increased systemic exposure and plasma half-life in mice.

item.title: Isocaloric substitution of plant-based for animal-based protein and physical fitness in adolescents: a cross-sectional study from the EHDLA study
item.description: CONCLUSION: In adolescents, modeled isocaloric substitutions between plant- and animal-derived protein sources were not associated with overall physical fitness, although food-level analyses showed heterogeneous associations, suggesting the relevance of the broader food matrix.

item.title: Harnessing bridge resonance to optimise multiexciton evolution through intramolecular singlet fission
item.description: The central question in the study of singlet fission remains how to control the interchromophore couplings that govern the formation, spin evolution and decay of triplet pairs through molecular design. In intramolecular singlet fission materials, this control is achieved by tethering chromophores with a range of bridging units. item.title: Molecular mechanisms of AcrVA-mediated Cas12a inhibition and their potential applications
item.description: CRISPR-Cas12a is widely used for genome editing because it is simple, efficient, and suitable for multiplex targeting. However, strong or prolonged Cas12a activity can increase unwanted cleavage at off-target sites. This problem is especially important when Cas12a is used in complex microbial communities, where unintended editing may affect non-target microorganisms or mobile genetic elements. Anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins are natural inhibitors of CRISPR-Cas systems. Acr proteins targeting type...

item.title: The animal is not only a reservoir: rabies and the limits of one health
item.description: Rabies demonstrates both the value and the limitations of the One Health approach as a public-health framework. Although mass dog vaccination and timely post-exposure prophylaxis can prevent human deaths, surveillance frequently underestimates disease burden, while control programs may treat dogs primarily as reservoirs or population denominators. Drawing together natural science, history, and anthropology, and narrating a remembered encounter with a rabid community dog named Lucky, this...

item.title: Which ARPI first in chemotherapy-naïve mCRPC? Enzalutamide versus abiraterone: A nationwide real-world study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of enzalutamide as the first ARPI was associated with improved survival, particularly in older and more comorbid patients. These findings suggest that treatment strategy should primarily focus on the selection of the first ARPI rather than on the sequencing of subsequent ARPIs.

item.title: Justicia procumbens suppresses high-fat diet-induced weight gain in mice and adipogenesis in 3T3-L1 cells with inhibition of AKT and STAT3 phosphorylation
item.description: Obesity is a major public health concern, and the long-term use of current pharmacological therapies can be constrained by adverse effects. Therefore, natural products with potential applicability to obesity management are of growing interest. Here, we investigated the anti-obesity effects of an extract of Justicia procumbens (JE), a traditionally used medicinal plant, and its underlying mechanisms. Oral administration of JE in a high-fat diet-induced obese mouse model significantly reduced body...

item.title: Association between childhood Taekwondo duration and adult participation intention among South Korean university students: a cross-sectional study
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Sport participation during childhood and adolescence is associated with physical activity in adulthood, yet how participation in a specific sport relates to adult participation patterns remains unclear. In South Korea, Taekwondo participation is concentrated in childhood and declines across the transition to adulthood. This cross-sectional study examined whether childhood Taekwondo duration was associated with adult participation time and participation intention in Taekwondo, other...

item.title: High-frequency conductivity was negatively associated with myelin water fraction in the brain of cognitive impairments
item.description: CONCLUSION: Lower apparent MWF was associated with higher HFC, suggesting a relationship between tissue microstructural alterations and conductivity. Further research is needed to validate these findings in diverse populations.

item.description: Pain in the posterior buttock and posterolateral thigh has many possible sources, including the spine, the sciatic nerve, the hip, and local muscles, tendons, and fascia. On the posterolateral femur, the distal insertion of the gluteus maximus and the origin of the short head of the biceps femoris converge with the iliotibial band and the lateral intermuscular septum. We refer to this region as the gluteobicipital posterolateral femoral myofascial-entheseal complex, an operational descriptive...

item.title: Delegated precision: a predictive-processing hypothesis on external affective labeling and self-interpretation
item.description: Predictive-processing accounts describe affective inference as the integration of bodily evidence and learned expectations. Emotion-aware systems increasingly supply affective labels during that process. This Hypothesis and Theory article asks when repeated external interpretation changes subsequent self-interpretation, rather than merely adding a useful cue. We propose delegated precision as a conditional, history-dependent alteration in uncertainty about the reliability of endogenous affective...

item.title: Psychometric Evaluation of the Korean Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire: Evidence of Measurement Invariance and Sex-Related Camouflaging Patterns
item.description: Social camouflaging involves complex strategies used to navigate social challenges, which are increasingly recognized across varying levels of autistic traits. Despite its clinical importance in explaining diagnostic disparities, no validated measure exists in Korea. This study evaluated the psychometric properties and factor structure of the Korean version of the Camouflaging Autistic Traits Questionnaire (CAT-Q) across levels of autistic traits. item.title: Weight- and age-dependent bias in remimazolam pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models during bispectral index-guided anesthesia: a retrospective analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Body weight and age significantly modify the Ce-BIS relationship in remimazolam-based anesthesia, with negative bias observed across all four PKPD models in low-body-weight older patients. These findings warrant prospective validation in larger and more diverse cohorts and remimazolam PKPD model refinement that adequately incorporates body size and age.

item.title: Prior stroke history and functional outcomes after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: An exploratory propensity score-adjusted analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The crude association between prior stroke history and poor functional outcome was substantially attenuated after adjustment for measured confounders. Prior stroke history alone should not drive prognostic judgment; acute severity and premorbid functional status should also be considered. These exploratory findings require multicenter validation.

Clinical data from patients with molecularly confirmed S-RMS treated at 25 institutions between January 2013 and December 2023 were reviewed. Endpoints included overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall response rate...

item.title: Violence Prevention Climate in Korean Hospitals: Associations With Nurses' Workplace Violence Experiences and Organizational Citizenship Behavior
item.description: CONCLUSION: The Korean version of the Violence Prevention Climate Scale showed promising evidence of validity and reliability for assessing organizational violence prevention efforts among Korean nurses, although structural validity requires further confirmation. Strengthening the violence prevention climate may help reduce workplace violence and promote prosocial behavior that supports high-quality care.

item.title: Regulatory T and Activated T Cells in the Chronic Unpredictable Mild Stress Mice: Sex Differences and Effects of Treatments
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study highlights that curcumin, simvastatin, fluoxetine, and SAMe alleviate depressive-like behaviors, while SAMe also reduces the CD154/CD152 ratio. These findings reveal marked sex differences in T-cell activation and immune regulation, highlighting the importance of considering sex as a biological variable in CUMS research.

item.title: Feasibility of prior-informed domain-based electrical impedance tomography for deep tissue thermometry: Phantom experiments and computed tomography-derived numerical simulations
item.description: CONCLUSION: The proposed domain-based EIT thermometry demonstrated feasibility in phantom experiments and a CT-derived anatomical model, establishing a foundation for its potential application as a non-invasive temperature monitoring approach.

item.title: Quality of life with first-line ribociclib plus endocrine therapy vs combination chemotherapy in clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC: RIGHT Choice
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with first-line ribociclib plus ET translates into improved QOL versus combination chemotherapy in patients with clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC. These data reinforce efficacy and safety findings supporting cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors plus ET as the preferred option in this population.

item.title: Equity in maternity care under universal health coverage: prenatal care utilization and obstetric outcomes among migrant women in Korea, 2022
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cross-sectional study, migrant women had lower prenatal care utilization but did not have higher odds of any obstetric complication than Korean women. Associations varied by specific complications and maternal age groups. Despite universal health coverage, persistent disparities in prenatal care utilization highlight the need to identify and address barriers to equitable maternity care for migrant women.

item.title: LDL-C-stratified residual lipoprotein(a) and inflammatory risk after acute myocardial infarction among patients with prior statin use
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AMI despite documented prior statin exposure, the prognostic associations of residual inflammatory and Lp(a) risk appeared to differ across admission LDL-C strata, supporting the potential value of LDL-C-stratified residual risk assessment.

item.title: Multidisciplinary perspectives on digital healthcare for people with disabilities: a qualitative study using a role-centered matrix approach
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings provide an expert-derived conceptual model rather than a definitive service specification. Two unresolved issues are particularly important for the intended users: accommodating variation within the population and exercising access rights when capacity to consent is in question. Validation and co-design with people with lived experience of disability are necessary next steps.

item.description: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA/MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic-inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. item.description: The current understanding of zeolite crystallization is still far from well understood. Herein, we show that the crystallization pathway of high-silica ZSM-5, one of the most industrially important zeolites, can be altered not only by the type of organic structure-directing agents (OSDAs) at a gel Si/Al ratio of 50 but also by the simultaneous use of Na+ and Cs+ ions as inorganic structure-directing agents (ISDAs). item.title: Evaluation of the eating quality traits in β-amylase (OsBMY7) mutant lines derived from the japonica rice cultivar Koshihikari
item.description: Endosperm β-amylase (BMY) in rice releases maltose from non-reducing ends of starch and is expected to contribute to cooked rice eating quality through its action during grain filling and cooking. However, the impact of specific BMY mutations on eating quality-related traits remains unclear. item.title: Macular Vortex Veins in Idiopathic Choroidal Neovascularization: A Pilot Case Series
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: MVVs were more frequently observed in eyes with idiopathic type 2 CNV than in healthy eyes. Given the small sample and retrospective design, these findings are hypothesis-generating. Larger, modality-matched studies are needed to determine whether MVVs have pathophysiologic relevance.

item.description: Internal functionalization can reorganize intermolecular interactions across a self-assembled monolayer (SAM), yet its depth-dependent consequences remain poorly understood. item.title: Care processes and 1-year outcomes following Japan's hip fracture payment reform: the LIFE Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Japan's hip fracture reimbursement reform was associated with improved care processes, but not with better 12-month outcomes. Broader implementation support and longer follow-up may be needed to assess effects on patient outcomes.

item.description: Many environmental bacteria do not readily grow under laboratory conditions, and population establishment often occurs stochastically. Although the scout hypothesis has been proposed to explain stochastic population establishment in environmental bacteria, how stochastic population establishment is shaped by individual cell growth behaviors in environmental isolates remains unclear. item.title: Charcot-Leyden crystals drive a localized inflammatory niche around mucus plugs in Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: CLC-containing mucus plugs form focal inflammatory niches in acute ABPA, and experimental CLC deposition is sufficient to promote persistent airway obstruction and inflammation. These findings identify CLCs as a biomarker, imaging target, and tractable therapeutic target in eosinophilic muco-obstructive airway disease.

item.title: Longitudinal analysis of email-based consultation support for gastrointestinal stromal tumor in Japan
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: GIST-related email consultations showed a shift from professional inquiries about diagnosis and drug development to patient- and family-centered needs regarding standard treatment and specialist access during the past two decades. Effective email consultation requires sufficiently precise clinical information.

item.title: From Sensor Design to Force Maps: A Systematic Evaluation of Förster Resonance Energy Transfer-Based Tension Probes
item.description: Mechanical forces transmitted through focal adhesions regulate cell behavior and disease progression, yet remain difficult to quantify at the molecular level. Genetically encoded FRET-based tension probes enable measurements of piconewton-scale forces across specific proteins in living cells, but their quantitative interpretation is highly sensitive to probe design and measurement modality. item.title: Association between aortic arch atheroma and periprocedural stroke following transcatheter aortic valve implantation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Aortic arch atheroma severity was associated with an increased risk of periprocedural stroke following transfemoral-TAVI, with the impact being more pronounced in patients treated with SE-THV than in those treated with BE-THV.

item.title: Prognostic impact of new-onset left bundle branch block after transcatheter aortic valve replacement according to preoperative diastolic dysfunction severity
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: New-onset LBBB was associated with worse outcomes after TAVR, especially in grade 2-3 DD. DD grading may help identify patients more susceptible to adverse impact of new-onset LBBB.

item.title: Clinical practical advice for anaesthetic management of adults with congenital heart disease undergoing non-cardiac surgery: A clinical consensus statement of the ESC Working Group on Adult Congenital Heart Disease, the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care, the European Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care and the International Society of Adult Congenital Heart Disease
item.description: Adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) patients often require non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and the need of such interventions is growing as the population ages. item.description: Cells migrate with varying degrees of polarization and directional persistence as exemplified by epithelial, mesenchymal and amoeboid cell types. Depending on the physiological and developmental context, these states are often interchangeable, reflecting the plastic and adaptive nature of the cytoskeleton. item.description: Minimally invasive esophagectomy is becoming the preferred approach in the treatment with curative-intent of esophageal cancer. Consequently, upper gastrointestinal surgeons in training are less exposed to open esophagectomy during their training. However, some patients or tumors are not eligible for minimally invasive surgery or require alternative reconstructive options, risking referral to nonsurgical therapies. item.description: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation offers a sustainable route to reductive molecular transformations by generating hydrogen equivalents from water under ambient conditions. item.title: Recognizing peer support initiatives organized outside of the clinical setting: insights from a Belgian Delphi method with peer supporters, patients, and mental health professionals
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Peer-led, non-clinical peer support represents a valuable complement to the recovery-oriented mental health landscape in Belgium. However, its sustainable integration requires strengthening recognition and support structures while preserving the core values of mutuality, authenticity, and lived experience. The findings highlight a central challenge for the field: balancing professionalization with the preservation of the relational and experiential foundations that underpin peer...

item.title: Rapid progression of myocardial calcification in a patient presenting with hypercalcemia of unidentified etiology: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Severe hypercalcemia of unidentified etiology can be complicated by extensive myocardial calcification. Ectopic calcification initially induced by hypercalcemia may have been influenced by inflammatory conditions such as eosinophilia. In addition, subsequent myocardial injury may accelerate dystrophic calcification. Clinicians should be aware of the risk of early and progressive cardiac involvement in patients with hypercalcemia, particularly in the presence of inflammatory...

item.title: Emergency resection of a ruptured mediastinal mature teratoma with cranial inflammatory spread along the anterior visceral space
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Ruptured mediastinal teratoma may rarely present with cervical inflammation caused by cranial spread along the anterior visceral space. Even in the absence of overt airway obstruction, the potential risk of airway compromise should be assessed individually when determining the timing of surgical treatment.

item.description: Associations between dizziness symptoms and psychological factors have been reported, but evaluating this through questionnaires alone risks recall bias. item.description: Laccases (EC 1.10.3.2) are multicopper oxidases that oxidize diverse phenolic and non-phenolic compounds while reducing oxygen to water. Despite their highly conserved catalytic architectures, fungal laccases perform diverse biological functions depending on ecological context. In saprophytic fungi, they contribute to lignin degradation, nutrient acquisition, carbon cycling, and pollutant detoxification, supporting their application in bioremediation, wastewater treatment, biofuel production,...

item.title: Plant pathogenic continuum in the microbiome era
item.description: Plant pathology has traditionally relied on a binary distinction between pathogens and non-pathogens, or between harmful and beneficial microorganisms. However, this distinction is becoming increasingly difficult to maintain in the microbiome era. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic HF phenotypes are characterized by distinct and shared DNA methylation signatures. These epigenetic profiles reflect relevant biological pathways and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes, supporting their potential utility in HF risk stratification and precision medicine.

item.title: Pulmonary Artery Pressures Predict Heart Failure Events Following Heart Failure and Non-Heart Failure Events
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Persistently elevated PAP early after discharge following either an index non-HFE or an HFE is associated with the risk of a subsequent HFE. (Hemodynamic-GUIDEd Management of Heart Failure [GUIDE-HF]; NCT03387813).

item.title: Quantity and quality of children's screen use and their neural and associated behavioral outcomes: A systematic review
item.description: The developmental impact of screen use on young children remains an active area of inquiry, with evidence of both risks and benefits depending on quantity and quality of exposure. item.description: Background: Neurosteroids, such as pregnenolone, have potential in mood disorder treatment. item.description: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is critical for inflammatory responses to cytosolic DNA. item.description: CONCLUSION: Loneliness and social isolation are associated with increased mortality in individuals with T2DM. Social isolation is particularly detrimental for men, and risks are heightened in older adults. Incorporating assessment of social disconnection into diabetes care may help identify vulnerable groups and inform targeted interventions to reduce premature mortality.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This outbreak might not have been detected without surveillance testing of pet food products for enteric pathogens. Outbreaks related to dry pet food can be protracted because of the extended shelf life of these products. Enteric pathogens that contaminate pet products can result in infant illness. It is important to educate caregivers about the importance of handwashing after feeding pets and the proper ways to clean and disinfect pet feeding equipment.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Fungal mortality remained elevated after the COVID-19 pandemic peak despite declines in COVID-19-associated fungal deaths. item.title: Interleukin-8 levels partially account for the indirect relationship between alcohol use disorder and global sleep quality in a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that AUD diagnosis is associated with worse sleep, partially through an association with greater IL-8 levels. Identifying a role for IL-8 as a link between AUD and sleep disturbance will need to be tested in longitudinal studies. If replicated, IL-8 inhibition may offer a novel treatment target for those with AUD and comorbid sleep disorders. This article is part of the Sleep and Circadian Mechanisms in Mental Health Collection.

item.title: The Lactate-Lactylation Axis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Biological Functions, Tumor Microenvironment, and Therapeutic Implications
item.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with metabolic reprogramming, epigenetic dysregulation, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) contributing to disease progression and treatment challenges.
